item.text: The CCC audited how five Queensland councils administered councillor discretionary funds, focusing on accountability, transparency and corruption risks.
item.support: To examine five selected councils and determine if they were effectively administering councillor discretionary funds

item.text: It also assessed how two public authorities handled corruption allegations concerning grants and funding.
item.support: To assess whether the Department of Local Government, Racing and Multicultural Affairs, and Redland City Council had dealt with allegations

item.text: The CCC identified 11 areas needing improvement, including incomplete applications, conflicts of interest and monitoring of spending.
item.support: The CCC observed 11 areas for improvement across the five councils.

item.text: The CCC was satisfied with the handling of the seven complaints it reviewed.
item.section: Agencies’ dealings with allegations of corrupt conduct
item.support: had dealt effectively with the seven complaints of corrupt conduct relating to grants and funding activities.

item.text: It recommended improvements to council controls and moving discretionary funding into community grants programs with stronger assessment rules.
item.support: the funds could be moved into specific community grants programs that require more robust guidelines

item.quote: The expenditure of funds at each councillor’s discretion created obvious risks in relation to the potential for fraud, corruption and abuse.
